name: page-tint-no-usable-colour
description:
neither a declared tag nor a favicon gives these pages a colour. Both declare no theme-color and carry the same all-white favicon, which the k-means lightness band refuses - a monochrome mark says nothing about its site that every other monochrome mark does not.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO PROVES CHANGED. The vlog below is now the load-bearing assertion: 'page tint sampled (none)' is the declared-and-favicon path finding nothing, which is what this scenario is about. The region assertion no longer measures the space theme, because the ambilight reads these pages' own light-grey pixels and tints toward them. It measures that the glow holds steady across a tab switch instead - which is worth keeping: the first version of that sampler skipped the repaint whenever a new page resolved the colours the old one had, and the chrome sat on the plain space tint until something happened to differ.

actions.note: let the first tab commit and its favicon resolve
the chrome while White One is in front

assertions.label: the-switch-really-happened
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL, and this scenario is worthless without it: region_stable passes for free when the tab switch never happened. That trap bit a partner scenario's first draft.

assertions.label: neither-tag-nor-favicon-gave-a-colour
assertions.desc: Itself: the declared-tag path found no theme-color and the favicon path refused the all-white mark, so that half of the sampler resolved nothing. This is what the region assertion used to stand in for, and it says it directly.

THE MEASUREMENT: the glow beside the card held steady across the switch. ambilight-paints-the-near-edge reads 22.62 across this same region when the left edge really changes, so 3 is a ceiling the feature clears by an order of magnitude when it has a reason to move.
assertions.note: The band the glow paints: 32 DIP out from the card's left edge at about x=225 in the VM frame, at 55 percent of the glass alpha. Re-measured 2026-08-27 when the glow was narrowed and dimmed.
